skeleton:
Dfina Sabbath Stew

Moroccan · Medium · Serves 6–8

Jump to Recipe Method Troubleshooting Storage
The dfina — Morocco's Jewish community's overnight stew, the Sephardic hamin's Moroccan seat — is the Sabbath's own engineering: a pot assembled Friday before sundown and left to cook through the night at the oven's dying warmth or the coals' ash, so that no fire is touched on the day of rest and the table at Saturday noon receives a pot that has become stew, broth, and bread in one. The beans and the eggs and the wheat berries — the whole canon's constants — and the record that carries this site's whole Sephardic block's (#61–90's) founding doctrine: the long overnight clock, the sealed pot, and the faith that heat's absence can cook as truly as heat's presence.

Quantities live in the recipe card.

Ingredients

  • the dfina's signature (they cook in the pot and are served peeled, browned by the broth's slow osmosis)

The kouglas (the Sabbath's dumplings, optional and beloved)

  • kneaded 5 minutes, formed to small flat cakes, and buried in the pot (they cook in the broth's steam to a dense, satisfying bread)

To serve

: the #73 huevos haminados doctrine's whole-wheat bread, the #104 pickled turnips, and the harissa (#91) at the table

- **Assemble before the sundown — the overnight clock is the recipe.** The dfina's oven runs its lowest (90–110 °C) or the pot sits in the banked coals' ash; the hours (10 to 12) are the cook, and the pot is sealed with a tight lid or foil so the steam's return is entire. The faith's engineering: the fire is not touched, and the low heat's patience does everything. - **The bridge:** the eggs in the shell are the dfina's own — the #73 huevos haminados carries their full doctrine (the slow-cooked whites browned to amber, the yolks creamed) — and no dfina is served without them. The wheat berries bridge to the pearl barley's quicker clock honestly; the kouglas are optional and the pot's own luxury.

Doneness & Quality Checkpoints

  • The Friday assembly: seasoned one notch past, sealed tight, the eggs in their shells.
  • The overnight: 10–12 hours untouched at the dying warmth.
  • The Saturday opening: the beef at the spoon's suggestion, the eggs' whites amber.

Dfina Sabbath Stew

Prep: 30 minutes (Friday) · Cook: 12 hours overnight, untouched · Total: From Friday evening to Saturday noon · Serves 6–8

Ingredients

Ingredients

  • 800 g beef on the bone (shank or short rib), cut to large pieces
  • 200 g wheat berries, soaked 8 hours (or the #36's couscous's large-pearl register); 150 g chickpeas, soaked 8 hours
  • 6 eggs in their shells, washed — the dfina's signature (they cook in the pot and are served peeled, browned by the broth's slow osmosis)
  • 3 onions (about 450 g): two whole and quartered, one minced fine for the kouclas (below)
  • 1 head garlic (about 30 g), halved across; a fist of parsley (about 20 g), tied
  • 1 tbsp paprika; 2 tsp cumin; 1 tsp turmeric; ½ tsp cinnamon; ½ tsp black pepper; 1½ tsp salt
  • 3 tbsp olive oil (about 40 g); water to cover generously (about 2.5 litres)

The kouglas (the Sabbath's dumplings, optional and beloved)

  • 200 g flour, 1 tsp salt, and water to a stiff dough — kneaded 5 minutes, formed to small flat cakes, and buried in the pot (they cook in the broth's steam to a dense, satisfying bread)

To serve

    Instructions

    1. **The Friday assembly (20 minutes).** Combine the beef, the soaked wheat and chickpeas, the quartered onions, the garlic, the herbs, the spices, the oil, and the salt in the heavy pot or Dutch oven; the eggs (in their shells) nestled among the meat; the water poured to cover generously. The kouglas cakes (if running) buried in the liquid's upper third. The lid sealed tight (foil's crimp beneath the lid for the sure seal). Checkpoint — the pot's broth tasted raw: one notch past salted (the long night's concentration calms) and the spices forward — the dfina's seasoning is all at the start, for no hand touches the pot again until noon.
    2. **The overnight (10–12 hours at the dying warmth).** Into the 100 °C oven (or the coals' ash equivalent) from Friday evening: 10 to 12 hours, untouched, unopened — the faith's own clock. The pot's murmur is a murmur of hours; the eggs brown in their shells, the wheat berries swell to their chew, the beef surrenders to the spoon. Checkpoint — the Saturday opening (the pot's own theater): the broth runs deep brown and runs thick with the night's slow reduction; the beef falls at the spoon's mere suggestion; the eggs' shells peeled to reveal the amber whites and the creamed yolks (#73's own proof); the wheat berries swollen-tender with their nut-chew held; the kouglas dense and broth-perfumed. The kitchen smells like Saturday itself.
    3. **The noon table (10 minutes).** The pot to the table's center: the broth ladled deep into bowls, the beef and the wheat and the kouglas in each; an egg (or its half) in every bowl; the pickles and the harissa beside, and the bread for the sopping. Checkpoint — eating test: the broth's overnight depth — every element's flavor married through the hours — the beef's silk and the wheat's chew, the egg's amber-sliced richness over the bowl, the pickle's cut between the spoonfuls. It should taste like the Sabbath's own argument: the work finished before the rest, and the rest's patience the finest cook in the canon.

    Finish & Plate

    The pot to the table's center — the broth's brown, the beef's fall, the wheat's chew, the eggs' amber halved in every bowl — the pickles and the harissa at the table, and the Sabbath's own service: the work long finished, the table already blessed.

    Troubleshooting

    SymptomCauseFix
    Pot ran dry overnightHeat too high or the seal leaked100 \u00b0C's hold; the foil's crimp; water generous at the start
    Beef held its shape at noonThe heat ran too lowThe full clock; the dying-warmth's honest check
    Eggs' whites paleThe pot boiled (the fast whites)The overnight's gentle hold \u2014 the amber is the proof

    Storage, Make-Ahead & Variations

    - The dfina is the make-ahead by its own definition; the leftover pot keeps 2 days refrigerated and the eggs, peeled, are the finest lunch the canon offers. The #73 huevos haminados is the eggs' own record. - Variations: the #65 skhina's chestnut-sweet register, the #72 adafina's chickpea-forward ancestor. This record is the Sephardic block's foundation; the block's whole row carries its dials.
